record.paper_title: Erdős-Macintyre type theorem’s for multiple Dirichlet series: exceptional sets and open problems
record.original_question: Let p≥1 and let F∈D_p(λ^p) be an entire function on C^p represented by an absolutely convergent multiple Dirichlet series F(z)=∑_{n∈Z_+^p} a_n exp(<z,λ_n>). For x∈R^p define M(x,F)=sup{|F(x+iy)|: y∈R^p}, m(x,F)=inf{|F(x+iy)|: y∈R^p}, and μ(x,F)=max{|a_n|exp(<x,λ_n>) : n∈Z_+^p}. Given a positive differentiable function h:R_+→R_+ with h'(t) increasing to +∞, what conditions on F and its exponent system λ^p guarantee that M(x,F)=(1+o(1))μ(x,F) and M(x,F)=(1+o(1))m(x,F) hold as |x|→∞ outside some set E with finite h–τ_p measure ∫_E h'(|x|) dx_1...dx_p/|x|^(p−1)<∞?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer $p\ge 1$. Let $\lambda^p=(\lambda_n)_{n\in\mathbb{Z}_+^p}\subset\mathbb{R}_+^p$ be a system of exponents, and let $F\colon\mathbb{C}^p\to\mathbb{C}$ be an entire function representable by an absolutely convergent multiple Dirichlet series
$$F(z)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}_+^p} a_n\exp(\langle z,\lambda_n\rangle),\qquad z\in\mathbb{C}^p,$$
where $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ denotes the standard inner product on $\mathbb{R}^p$. Denote by $\mathcal{D}_p(\lambda^p)$ the class of all such entire functions. For $x\in\mathbb{R}^p$ define
$$M(x,F)=\sup_{y\in\mathbb{R}^p}|F(x+iy)|,\quad m(x,F)=\inf_{y\in\mathbb{R}^p}|F(x+iy)|,\quad \mu(x,F)=\max_{n\in\mathbb{Z}_+^p}|a_n|\exp(\langle x,\lambda_n\rangle).$$
Let $h\colon\mathbb{R}_+\to\mathbb{R}_+$ be a positive differentiable function whose derivative $h'(t)$ is increasing and tends to $+\infty$ as $t\to\infty$. For a measurable set $E\subset\mathbb{R}^p$, define its $h$–$\tau_p$ measure by
$$\tau_p^h(E)=\int_E \frac{h'(|x|)}{|x|^{p-1}}\,dx_1\cdots dx_p.$$

Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on $F\in\mathcal{D}_p(\lambda^p)$ and on the exponent system $\lambda^p$ under which both asymptotic relations
$$M(x,F)=(1+o(1))\,\mu(x,F)\quad\text{and}\quad M(x,F)=(1+o(1))\,m(x,F)$$
hold as $|x|\to\infty$ with $x$ ranging outside some exceptional set $E\subset\mathbb{R}^p$ of finite $h$–$\tau_p$ measure, i.e. $\tau_p^h(E)<\infty$.
